guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers lean toward West Virginia because we see more passing upside than its run-heavy profile might suggest. West Virginia logged 229 rushes against only 65 pass attempts through four games, but it also averaged 17 yards per completion and converted 53.2% of its third downs. Against a Cincinnati pass defense our metrics rate as vulnerable, that gives West Virginia another route to sustaining drives and creating explosive plays.

The concern for us is the other side of the matchup. Cincinnati has been effective at creating scoring opportunities, while West Virginia allowed 282.3 passing yards per game through four contests. Oklahoma State then threw for 389 yards with five completions gaining at least 27 yards. We are not treating one game as proof, but it reinforces a broader weakness Cincinnati can attack. That defensive vulnerability keeps our modest disagreement with the market from becoming enough value for a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching West Virginia’s passing game against Cincinnati’s pass defense. The offense has been built around the ground game, but our matchup numbers suggest West Virginia may not need to remain quite so run-dependent here. The question is whether it can turn favorable passing situations into enough explosive gains to offset the opportunities its own defense is likely to allow.

recent_game.fact: West Virginia lost 41-24 to Oklahoma State on Sept. 26, falling to 3-1 overall and 0-1 in the Big 12.
West Virginia rushed 66 times for 335 yards against Oklahoma State but completed 10 of 22 passes for 132 yards with one interception.
Cam Cook rushed 29 times for 193 yards against Oklahoma State, including a 75-yard run.
Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. rushed 28 times for 103 yards and three touchdowns against Oklahoma State while passing for 132 yards.
West Virginia allowed Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker to pass for 389 yards and three touchdowns, including completions of 52, 48, 48, 28 and 27 yards.
Oklahoma State outscored West Virginia 13-0 in the fourth quarter.

quarterback.fact: Michael Hawkins Jr. started each of West Virginia's first four games of 2026.
Hawkins and Cam Cook each exceeded 100 rushing yards in three of West Virginia's first four games.
